questions.stem: A 28-year-old man with a history of current intravenous drug use presents with fevers and chills for the past 4 days. On arrival, his vital signs are a temperature is 101.3°F (38.5°C ), a pulse of 110 beats per minute, a blood pressure of 90/60 mm Hg, a respiratory rate of 14 breaths per minute, and an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. He reports rigors and malaise but is otherwise asymptomatic. Initial blood cultures grow methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. The patient is treated with intravenous fluids and started on appropriate antibiotics with subjective improvement in his symptoms. On the following morning, he develops acute shortness of breath. A lung examination is notable for diffuse crackles over both lung fields. Cardiac auscultation reveals a new-onset loud diastolic murmur at the upper right sternal border. Which of the following is most likely responsible for this patient’s deterioration?
